What If You Were Stuck in the Emptiest Place in the Universe?

Episode 47 of a daily journey through the universe. 🕳️
The Boötes Void: a nearly empty region of space about 330 million light-years across, discovered in 1981, with only around 60 galaxies where there should be thousands. How voids form in the cosmic web.

segments.text: What if you were stuck in the emptiest place in the universe? You wouldn't see a single galaxy for years.
Galaxies aren't spread evenly. They form a giant web, with long threads of galaxies, and huge empty bubbles in between.
segments.headline: The cosmic web

segments.text: In nineteen eighty-one, astronomers looking toward the constellation Boötes found one of the biggest empty bubbles known.
segments.headline: Toward Boötes

segments.text: It's about three hundred thirty million light-years across.
A region that size should hold thousands of galaxies. The Boötes void has only about sixty.
If our Milky Way were in the middle of it, we wouldn't have known other galaxies existed until the nineteen sixties.
segments.headline: A lonely view

segments.text: Some people joked it was a place emptied by aliens. The real answer is gravity.
segments.headline: Not aliens

segments.text: After the Big Bang, matter was spread almost evenly. Slightly denser spots pulled in more and more. Slightly emptier spots kept emptying.
segments.headline: Gravity did it

segments.text: Over billions of years, small differences grew into the threads and voids we see today.
segments.headline: Billions of years

segments.text: Tomorrow, something huge is pulling our galaxy, and we can't see it. Next stop: the Great Attractor. Which part surprised you most? Tell me in the comments, and follow for tomorrow's stop.
